item.title: The SB Residency: Endless Summer, Montecito Edition
item.description: Montecito by the numbers. Priced right, gone in a week. Priced hopeful, priced again. Plus three listings that caught my eye.
item.content:encoded:
This issue is all Montecito, with one detour over the line. The calendar says October, the thermometer disagrees, and the market had a split personality this quarter. Let's get into it.

The Nitty Gritty

This issue's market, by the numbers.

Priced right, gone in a week. Priced hopeful, priced again. 8 of 38 Montecito homes sold in seven days or less, and 7 of those 8 closed at or above their original asking price. The 11 that sat past 100 days? They closed at a median of 82.5% of their original price, and every one of them closed at least 8% under. Same market, two very different outcomes. The difference was day-one pricing.

Montecito, single family homes

Closed sales, MLS District 10 (Montecito). Source: FLEX MLS.

  • Jul 13 to Oct 11, 2026 (90 days): 38 sales, median price $5,292,500, median 64 days on market
  • Sale price vs. list: homes closed at a median of 95.6% of their final list price, and 90.6% of their original list price
  • Sold in a week or less: 8 homes, 7 of them at or above original asking price
  • On the market more than 100 days: 11 homes, closing at a median of 82.5% of original asking price
  • Where the sales landed: 18 under $5M, 11 from $5M to $10M, and 9 at $10M and up. The top sale was $19.5M. No single outlier is driving the median this window.

Inventory snapshot (as of Oct 12, 2026)

  • Single family homes: 75 active, roughly 5.9 months of supply at the current pace

How I counted: closed single family sales in MLS District 10 (Montecito), July 13 to October 11, 2026. The district includes some homes with Santa Barbara mailing addresses. Condos are excluded. Three duplicate co-listing records and four closings that appear to be off-market deals (one day on market) are excluded. All figures are medians, not averages. "Original asking price" is the first list price. The active count removes six co-listing duplicates and one fractional ownership share. Source: FLEX MLS, deemed reliable but not guaranteed.

Window Shopping

Some listings that caught my eye this issue.

Three this issue: Pepper Hill two ways, and one just over the line in Upper State.

1170 Glenview Road, Montecito: $14,250,000

4 bed, 5 bath, 5,664 sq ft on about 1.9 acres in the Pepper Hill enclave, built in 1970 and extensively remodeled. A single-level European villa with sweeping Pacific views, stone and slate, hand-applied plaster, and oak floors reclaimed from a monastery in France. Antique doors, mantels, and marble sinks sourced from across Europe. New to the market this month.

Listing courtesy of Nancy Hamilton, Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices. (MLS #26-3419)

346 Woodley Road, Montecito: $10,200,000

3 bed, 3 bath, 3,090 sq ft on about an acre, built in 1974. Same Pepper Hill enclave, opposite energy. Sculptural lines, big glass, and oversized double front doors that open to a coastal panorama. Mountain, ocean, and harbor views, every bedroom en suite, and an ocean-facing loggia.

Listing courtesy of Cristal Clarke, Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices. (MLS #26-3381)

3141 Calle Fresno, Santa Barbara: $2,995,000

The detour. 3 bed, 2 bath on about 0.19 of an acre in Upper State, built in 1945. A Craftsman inspired by the cottages of San Ysidro, with a stone hearth, Carrara marble, and an office or one-car garage. Out back: a saltwater pool, jacuzzi, outdoor kitchen, and firepit. Moments from Stevens Park and Upper State Street.

Listing courtesy of Erin Chadwick, Compass. (MLS #26-3384)

Quick note: none of the above are my listings, just three that caught my eye this issue. Full credit to the listing agents and offices named above.

This Issue's Vibe

Local adventurers, storytellers, eats & other must-follows.

Follow: @thesantabarbaraopen Pro beach volleyball at East Beach, with the AVP net up and the Channel Islands as the backdrop. If you've never watched the pros play on our sand, you're missing one of the best free shows in town. This year, Santa Barbara Volleyball Club, where I coach, was a sponsor, and our club helped work the event. Proud to see our players and families out there making it happen. Follow along for the next one.

Follow: @waylanwineco Brothers Brad and Greg Saarloos dreamed this one up on a flight home from France, after a trip spent visiting small family wineries. The name? Their middle names, Wayne and Alan, mashed together. Now it's one of the best tasting rooms on Grand Ave in Los Olivos: marble bar, hex tile, and a lineup that runs from Chenin Blanc to Syrah. Worth the drive over the pass.

House Radio

The soundtrack to the SB Residency, updated all the time.

Everything we're listening to here in Santa Barbara, updated all the time.

On repeat this issue: NoMBe. That's Noah McBeth, a classically trained pianist born in Germany who splits his time between LA and Hawaii. He calls his sound Electric Soul: indie, chillwave, and old-school soul in the same groove. Fun fact: Chaka Khan is his godmother. Two new adds to the playlist: "Wait," the slow burn, and "Summer's Gone" (with Thutmose), the perfect mid-October send-off for a town where summer doesn't really leave. Turn it up on the drive down Coast Village.

Listen on Spotify

Currently Obsessed With: The Road to Doomsday

Whatever's got my attention this cycle, tool, trend, or otherwise.

Laying low with the hot weather we've had. I love movies, so I've been watching the Marvel series in order, leading up to the December 18 release of their next movie, Avengers: Doomsday. It's been super fun to revisit some of the older movies, and watching them in story order has been fun to do. A great way to beat the heat and have some fun. They're mostly all on Disney+.

item.title: The SB Residency: Small Town, Small Sample
item.description: Carpinteria by the numbers, small sample and all: single family, condos, and four listings that caught my eye.
item.content:encoded:
This issue is all Carpinteria. Small town, small sample, and one story about why that matters before we get to the numbers.

The Nitty Gritty

This issue's market, by the numbers.

The story behind the title. Carpinteria closed 21 homes in the last 60 days. That is not a lot of data, and it means one sale can rewrite the headline. Case in point: one single family home closed at $15.8M this window. Count it, and the median single family price looks up 5% from the prior 60 days. Leave it out, and the market is flat. Same town, same two months, two different stories. So I split the data at $5M and told you how many sales sit above it, instead of letting one big closing do the talking.

Carpinteria, single family homes under $5M

Closed sales, City of Carpinteria. Source: FLEX MLS.

  • Jul 30 to Sep 27, 2026: 10 sales, median price $1,971,500, median 21 days on market
  • May 31 to Jul 29, 2026 (prior 60 days): 9 sales, median $1,975,000, median 8 days. Price is flat, down 0.2%.
  • Jul 30 to Sep 27, 2025 (same window last year): 9 sales, median $2,280,000, median 11 days. Price is down 13.5% year over year.

Carpinteria, single family homes $5M and up

One sale in each window: $15,813,013 this window, $6.2M in the prior 60 days, $6.34M a year ago. One sale is not a median, so I am giving you counts only.

Why condos are in this issue. In a town this size, condos are almost half the action. 10 of the 21 closings this window were condos. Leave them out and you are missing the entry point to Carpinteria, and often the most active part of the market.

Carpinteria, condos

Closed sales, City of Carpinteria. Source: FLEX MLS.

  • Jul 30 to Sep 27, 2026: 10 sales, median price $887,500, median 14 days on market
  • May 31 to Jul 29, 2026 (prior 60 days): 7 sales, median $730,000, median 69 days. Price is up about 22%.
  • Jul 30 to Sep 27, 2025 (same window last year): 9 sales, median $850,000, median 4 days. Price is up about 4% year over year.

Condos moved faster than the prior 60 days (14 days versus 69) at a higher price. Versus last year they are up slightly. With 7 to 10 sales per group, treat that as a direction, not a verdict.

Inventory snapshot (as of Sep 28, 2026)

  • Single family under $5M: 12 active, roughly 2.4 months of supply at the current pace
  • Single family $5M and up: 14 active. At one sale per 60 days, that is more than two years of supply.
  • Condos: 19 active, roughly 3.8 months of supply

How I counted: closed sales in the City of Carpinteria only. Single family includes Home/Estate and PUD property types. Manufactured homes are excluded. Two condo closings that appear to be off-market deals (one day on market) and one obvious data-entry error record are excluded. All figures are medians, not averages. The $5M split is my own line, drawn by price, not an MLS category. Sample sizes are small (7 to 10 sales per group), so a single sale can move a number. Source: FLEX MLS, deemed reliable but not guaranteed.

Window Shopping

Some listings that caught my eye this issue.

Four listings this issue: two in Carpinteria, two in Santa Barbara, and one that is a little out there.

74 Chase Drive, Santa Barbara: $2,549,000

3 bed, 4 bath, 1,803 sq ft on about a third of an acre, built in 1960. A terrace with a glass railing and a view to match.

Listing courtesy of McKenzie Duddy, Compass. (MLS #26-3246)

727 Garden Street, Santa Barbara: $4,400,000

The Crown of Downtown. A penthouse plus two office suites in the heart of Santa Barbara, and there is a lot going on here. The residence is approx. 4,369 sq ft with 4 bed and 2.5 bath, high ceilings, natural light, and mountain and city views. Four private patios with tall glass doors, three fireplaces, a dumbwaiter, electric shades, a spa, a sauna, and a laundry room. The two office suites (approx. 1,809 and 949 sq ft) are currently tenant occupied. Gated garage parking with 8 spaces, plus 2 separate enclosed resident spaces. Worth knowing: the property is on a ground lease with 30 years remaining.

Listing courtesy of Kevin Goodwin, Goodwin Properties. (MLS #26-3129)

4217 Avenue Del Mar, Carpinteria: $34,000,000

The crazy one. 9 bed, 10 bath, 7,954 sq ft on about an acre, built in 1958. For scale, the priciest Carpinteria sale of this whole window was $15.8M. This asks more than double that.

Listing courtesy of Eric Haskell, The Agency (MLS #26-3249), and Trevor Wright, The Beverly Hills Estates (MLS #26-2701).

3559 Padaro Lane, Carpinteria: $11,000,000

4 bed, 2 bath, 1,758 sq ft on about 0.22 of an acre, built in 1953. Oceanfront, and a bedroom with corner windows onto the water.

Listing courtesy of Gregg Leach, Village Properties. (MLS #26-3192)

Quick note: none of the above are my listings, just four that caught my eye this issue. Full credit to the listing agents and offices named above.

This Issue's Vibe

Local adventurers, storytellers, eats & other must-follows.

Follow: @santabarbarabodhipath A Buddhist center right here in Santa Barbara that hosts teachings and discussions. Worth a look if you are curious about the practice, or just want a calmer corner of your feed.

Follow: @stateofmind.sb A nonprofit cafe planned for downtown Santa Barbara, designed with and for the disability community. It plans to hire people with disabilities, host an arts hub with free space for local artists of all abilities, and put its profits back into local nonprofits. The target opening is December. Good one to know about early. More at stateofmindcafe.com.

House Radio

The soundtrack to the SB Residency, updated all the time.

Everything we're listening to here in Santa Barbara, updated all the time.

On repeat this issue: StigBar. Found them in a surf video while I was working, and I haven't stopped listening. It's a California beach sound that will have you grabbing your surfboard and beach gear and heading to your local surf break. Start with "Burning," then play "Something I Should Tell You."

Listen on Spotify

Currently Obsessed With: Crystal Cove

Whatever's got my attention this cycle, tool, trend, or otherwise.

We were down in Newport Beach for a family trip, celebrating my mom's birthday. My parents came up from San Diego, my brother and his family joined us, and Newport was a good place to meet in the middle. We stayed at Marriott's Newport Coast Villas, and on morning walks by myself and my brother and his wife, we stumbled upon a hidden gem called Crystal Cove.

Here is the thing. Down on the sand there is a row of little historic beach cottages you can actually rent. They date to the 1920s and 1930s, and the district has been on the National Register of Historic Places since 1979. There is a boardwalk, red bungalows, and two restaurants right there (the Beachcomber and the Shake Shack). I did not eat there, but my brother and his wife did, and they said it was really good.

Booking is challenging, and I will not pretend otherwise. But that is true of anything that is a great value, right on the water, with an atmosphere like that. You can get in. You just have to be persistent.

How it works:

  • Reservations go through ReserveCalifornia.com or by phone at 800.444.7275.
  • Bookings open on a six-month daily rolling window. Set a reminder for the day you want to book.
  • Stays are capped at seven nights per year.
  • Per the Conservancy's site as of September 2026, dorm-style rooms run about $55 to $161 a night and standard cottages about $300 to $354 a night, sleeping 4 to 9. Rates vary by season and exclude the 10% Newport Beach transient occupancy tax.

item.title: The SB Residency: Steady as She Goes
item.description: Santa Barbara City's market holds its pace this issue, plus three listings worth a second look and a garlic shrimp dinner on repeat.
item.content:encoded:
Santa Barbara isn't rushing anywhere, and neither should you. Here's what's actually happening in the city market, three homes worth a second look, and what's had my attention off the clock.

The Nitty Gritty

This issue's market, by the numbers.

Santa Barbara City, Single-Family Homes (August 10 to September 9, 2026, via FLEX MLS)

  • Median close price: $1,865,000, up about 5% from the prior 30 days.
  • Median days on market: 23
  • Active inventory: 217 single-family homes

Nothing dramatic here, and that's the story. Prices are ticking up a little, homes are moving at close to the same pace they were a month ago, and inventory's holding steady. No frenzy, no slowdown, just a market that knows what it's doing.

Stats reflect single-family homes in the City of Santa Barbara only, not condos, not the wider county.

Window Shopping

Some listings that caught my eye this issue.

1510 Franceschi Road: $3,595,000

Perched on the Riviera with south-facing views that run straight out to the Pacific. Vaulted ceilings, a chef's kitchen, and a private lower-level primary suite that opens right onto the gardens. 3 beds, 3 baths, 3,250 sqft on nearly half an acre. Listing courtesy of Chris Palme, Sotheby's International Realty. (MLS #26-3018)

1508 Miramar: $7,595,000

Sand-front on Miramar Beach, which is about as rare as it gets. Currently set up as a duplex, two private 1-bed/2-bath homes each with their own entrance and ocean views, with the option to convert back to a single residence. 2 beds, 4 baths, 1,550 sqft. Listing courtesy of Emily Gaul, Christie's International RE SoCal. (MLS #26-3022)

304 Sherwood Drive: $2,870,000

Tucked into a bamboo grove with koi ponds, wraparound ipe wood decking, and an imported Balinese tea house. This one's a meditation retreat that happens to have 3 beds and 2.5 baths. 2,948 sqft on 0.45 acres. Listing courtesy of Ali Evans, Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices California Properties. (MLS #26-3029)

Quick note: none of the above are my listings, just three that caught my eye this issue. Full credit to the listing agents and offices named above.

This Issue's Vibe

Local adventurers, storytellers, eats & other must-follows.

Follow: @ancoraosteria

New Italian spot from the Crestanelli brothers (the team behind S.Y. Kitchen) that just opened in Montecito's Upper Village. House-made pasta, Roman-style pinsa, and a wine list that runs from Italy to the Santa Ynez Valley. The meatballs alone are worth the drive.

Follow: @hacsbsantabarbara

The Housing Authority of the City of Santa Barbara does the unglamorous, essential work of keeping this town livable for the people who make it run. Worth a follow if you care about where SB is headed, not just what it's selling for.

House Radio

The soundtrack to the SB Residency, updated all the time.

Everything we're listening to here in Santa Barbara, updated all the time. Listen on Spotify

On repeat this issue: Sugar Water and Late Nights, both from Vatos Tristes. If you haven't come across them yet, they're an Elgin, Illinois band blending Midwest emo with Spanish hardcore and Latin influences (frontman Christian Cuellar calls it "Mexwestemo," which feels about right). The band started as a couple of guys jamming at community college and turned into a full lineup that's been packing rooms like Cobra Lounge and Lincoln Hall in Chicago. These two tracks are the ones I keep coming back to lately, good energy without being loud for the sake of being loud.

Currently Obsessed With: Camarones al Mojo de Ajo

Whatever's got my attention this cycle, tool, trend, or otherwise.

I've been on a real home cooking kick for a while now, and it's turned into one of my favorite parts of the week. There's something about standing at the stove after a full day of showings and calls that resets me. No rush, no phone, just garlic hitting hot oil.

This one's in heavy rotation lately. Garlicky, a little smoky from the dried chiles, finished with a good handful of cilantro right at the end. Pour it over Spanish rice so the rice soaks up all that sauce, and you've got a full dinner in about 25 minutes, start to finish. Every time I make this and post it, I get a couple DMs asking for the recipe, so figured I'd just make it official.

Here's the thing: most nights this beats going out. Less money, less waiting, and honestly better flavor since you control the heat and the garlic (a lot of garlic). But the real reason I keep making it isn't the shrimp. It's that cooking for my family is one of the easiest ways I know to show them I love them. Slow down, stand at the stove, put something good on the table. That's the whole game some nights.

If you've got a recipe you swear by, send it my way. Always looking for the next one.

item.title: The SB Residency: Steady in the Goodland
item.description: Days on market just hit a 12-month low in Goleta. Here's what's really moving in the Goodland right now, plus three properties worth a look.
item.content:encoded:
There's something satisfying about things being dialed in, whether it's a closet or a market. Homes here aren't just selling, they're selling fast, and there are more of them moving than any other month this year. No wild swings, no headlines, just a market that's quietly humming along. Here's what the numbers actually say, plus three places worth a second look (and a little organizing inspiration at the end).

The Nitty Gritty

This issue's market, by the numbers.

Goleta, Single-Family Homes (July 2026, via FLEX MLS)

  • Median sold price: $1,080,000
  • Active median list price: $1,410,000
  • Average days on market: 12.6 days, the fastest month of the past year. June was 24.5, and the 12-month average runs closer to 30.
  • Homes sold: 27, the highest monthly total in the past 12 months.
  • Active listings: 43

The read: Goleta's moving fast and moving more. July had the quickest average days on market and the most closed sales of any month in the past year. Pricing held basically flat year-over-year once you look past a low-volume comp month, this isn't a market getting away from anyone, it's one that's just efficient right now. If you're thinking about listing in the Goodland, this is a strong window: buyers are ready, and homes aren't sitting.

Stats reflect single-family homes in Goleta only, not condos, not the wider county. We rotate through a different market each issue.

Window Shopping

Some listings that caught my eye this issue.

3260 Polo Way, Carpinteria: $4,600,000

A new build, something genuinely rare to find in Santa Barbara County. Warm, open living with those signature exposed wood beams overhead and pocketing glass doors that erase the line between indoor and outdoor. Chef's kitchen, oak floors throughout, and a backyard built for actual living, not just looking at. 4 bed | 4.5 bath | 4,072 sqft. Listing courtesy of Calcagno & Hamilton Group, Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices California Properties. (MLS #26-2897)

531 Chapala Street Unit A, Santa Barbara: $3,300,000

An extraordinary live/work condo inside a courtyard development by famed architect Jeff Shelton, the same hand behind some of downtown's most recognizable tile and ironwork. Steps from State Street, this one's less "starter unit" and more "own a piece of a landmark." 1 bed | 1.5 bath | 2,231 sqft. Listing courtesy of Jason Saltoun-Ebin. (MLS #26-2702)

3061 Foothill Road, Santa Barbara: $1,595,000

A clean, single-level ranch with a dusk-lit curb appeal that photographs like it already knows it's the one. New landscaping, updated garage, move-in ready. 3 bed | 2 bath | 1,230 sqft. Listing courtesy of Candy Hedrick, Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices California Properties. (MLS #26-2901)

See something you like? Reach out and let's talk. Not my listings. Sharing because they caught my eye. I'm happy to show you any of these or find something that fits even better.

This Issue's Vibe

Local adventurers, storytellers, eats & other must-follows.

Follow: @themulletsb

The Mullet, a cocktail bar with a name and a sign that doesn't take itself too seriously. Good drinks, better people-watching.

Follow: @neighborhoodbunker

A golf simulator setup that'll make you want to build one in your own garage. Fitting, since this issue's obsession lives in a closet, not a course.

House Radio

The soundtrack to the SB Residency, updated all the time.

Everything we're listening to here in Santa Barbara, updated all the time. Listen on Spotify

On repeat this issue: Control World Demos by Feeble. Long before Blink-182, long before The Aquabats, Travis Barker's first punk band was this scrappy Fontana four-piece back in the mid-'90s. Deep teenage-years nostalgia territory, especially after the Travis Barker Netflix documentary sent everyone down the same rabbit hole. "Released" and their cover of "I Think We're Alone Now" are both sitting near the top of the SB Residency playlist right now, exactly what garage punk sounded like before any of it went mainstream.

Currently Obsessed With: Organization

Whatever's got my attention this cycle, tool, trend, or otherwise.

Full disclosure: this isn't really my idea. My wife works with Neat Method (@santabarbaraneat), the local organizing outfit that turns chaos into calm for a living, and she's been doing it to our house for years. I'm just finally keeping up.

Spent the last two weeks tearing into my own closet. Anything I don't wear, doesn't fit, or should've left the building years ago, gone. Turns out getting ruthless about what stays feels almost as good as buying something new.

The tool that made it stick: Essembl, an app that digitizes your closet, photo by photo, then uses AI to build outfits out of what you actually own. Once it's catalogued, it starts suggesting combinations you'd never have put together yourself.

Photo courtesy of Neat Method Santa Barbara (@santabarbaraneat).

Bigger picture: dialing in your space doesn't just make you more efficient, it clears out the noise in your head too. Less clutter in the closet, less clutter in the mind.

item.title: The SB Residency: Office Hours, Poolside
item.description: Montecito inventory is climbing and homes are sitting longer. Here's what that means, plus three properties worth a look.
item.content:encoded:
Just got back from Cancun with the family: new place, good sun, real time with Melissa and the kids. Still stayed dialed in with buyers and sellers the whole trip. That's Office Hours, Poolside in a nutshell: be present for your people wherever you are, and still show up for the ones counting on you back home. This issue's got a Montecito market check, three listings worth a second look, and what's been keeping me on track while I'm out there living it.

The Nitty Gritty

This issue's market, by the numbers.

Montecito, Single-Family Homes (July 2026, via FLEX MLS)

  • Median sold price: $5,422,500. Worth a caveat here: Montecito only sees about 10 sales a month, so the median swings hard. June came in at $8,675,000, and July last year was $9,500,000. The average sold price, $6,887,000, gives a steadier read.
  • Active listings: 53, up from 34 back in January. Inventory has been climbing steadily all year.
  • Average days on market: 74.4 days, more than double June's 35.4. Homes are sitting longer as more choices hit the market.
  • New listings: 21 in July, with 10 sold. Supply is outpacing demand right now.

The read: don't get hung up on the median swinging month to month, that's a small-sample market doing what small-sample markets do. The real story is inventory building since January while days on market climbs right along with it. More to choose from, more time to choose it. If you've been waiting for room to negotiate, this is what that looks like.

Stats reflect single-family homes in Montecito only, not condos, not the wider county. We rotate through a different market each issue.

Window Shopping

Some listings that caught my eye this issue.

3211 Padaro Lane, Carpinteria: $7,950,000

Not in Montecito, but it earns its spot this issue anyway. Coastal-close, quietly done, the kind of place that makes "working from home" sound pretty good. 4 bed | 4 bath | 2,305 sqft. Listing courtesy of Aaron Gilles, Village Properties. (MLS #26-2673)

2150 Ten Acre Road, Montecito: $5,795,000

This is the Office Hours, Poolside listing. Pool in the backyard, golf course right past the hedge, mountains behind that. Hard to imagine a bad day here. Casey and the Village Properties team also did a nice job with the virtual renderings on this one, worth a look at the listing to see what the space could become. 3 bed | 3.5 bath | 3,154 sqft. Listing courtesy of Casey Turpin, Village Properties. (MLS #26-2654)

135 Pomar Lane, Montecito: $6,060,000

Big oak trees, a courtyard built for lounging, and that classic Montecito quiet. The kind of outdoor living space that does most of the selling on its own. 3 bed | 3 bath. Listing courtesy of Marsha Kotlyar Estate Group, Berkshire Hathaway HomeServices. (MLS #26-2713)

See something you like? Reach out and let's talk. Not my listings. Sharing because they caught my eye. I'm happy to show you any of these or find something that fits even better.

This Issue's Vibe

Local adventurers, storytellers, eats & other must-follows.

Follow: @miliospizzasb

Margherita, blistered crust, fresh basil. Simple done right always wins.

Follow: @thelilliesummerland

A needlepoint, heirlooms, and mahjong studio tucked into Summerland. Part boutique, part hangout, exactly the kind of small-town gem that makes this stretch of coast worth slowing down for.

House Radio

The soundtrack to the SB Residency, updated all the time.

Everything we're listening to here in Santa Barbara, updated all the time. Listen on Spotify

On repeat this issue: 7 Seas by Dirty Heads. Huntington Beach's own reggae, hip-hop, and rock mashup dropped their ninth studio album this June, their first new full-length since 2022. The title track "Seven Seas" and the album opener are both sitting at the top of the SB Residency playlist right now. If you've followed these guys since "Lay Me Down," this one's a return to the sun-soaked, feel-good sound that made them SoCal staples in the first place.

Currently Obsessed With: My Personal Dashboard

Whatever's got my attention this cycle, tool, trend, or otherwise.

Built this myself using Claude and OpenClaw, and it's become the thing keeping me honest while I'm out here living the "Office Hours, Poolside" life. It tracks my goals, business and personal, and turns staying on track into something closer to a game than a chore. Even with the family time, the travel, and every other distraction vacation throws at you, I'm still hitting my numbers. Turns out a little gamification goes a long way.

If you're thinking about building your own: don't just track the big outcome numbers, track the daily actions that actually move them. A goal like "close more deals" is too far away to feel real every day. "Make one client touch" isn't. Pick a handful of daily actions across the areas that matter to you and let the streaks do the motivating. The scoreboard doesn't lie, and that's the point.

The other key is covering every part of your life, not just work. Mine is broken into a few buckets: work and money, health and energy, mind, and family and presence. If it only tracks the business side, you'll optimize for deals and quietly let everything else slide. Build it so all of it is in front of you at once.

And keep it everywhere. Mine's up on my phone, my home computer, and my laptop, so it's staying top of mind no matter where I am or what I'm doing. Out of sight is out of mind, and the whole point is that it never leaves your sight.

item.title: The SB Residency: Slim Pickings
item.description: Santa Barbara inventory is down 23% year-over-year. Here's what that means for buyers and sellers, plus three properties worth a look.
item.content:encoded:
Santa Barbara just hit the mid-year mark, and the story isn't "hot" or "cold." It's slim pickings. Active listings are down almost a quarter from a year ago, which is why we're calling this issue what it is. Fewer homes, faster sales, and buyers who show up ready to move. Here's what's actually happening on the ground, plus three places worth a second look.

The Nitty Gritty

This issue's market, by the numbers.

Santa Barbara City, Single-Family Homes (June 2026, via FLEX MLS)

  • Active listings: 201, down 23.3% year-over-year (262 in June 2025)
  • Median sold price: $1,712,500, down 6.2% year-over-year ($1,825,000 in June 2025), essentially flat to slightly softer, not a crash
  • Average days on market: 37.9 days, up 30.2% year-over-year (29.1 days in June 2025)

The read: inventory is the real story here. Down almost a quarter from a year ago, which is why homes are sitting a bit longer even as prices barely move. There's simply less to compete for. If you've been waiting for more choices to show up, they're not coming. If you've been sitting on the fence about listing, you're facing less competition than you were a year ago.

Stats reflect single-family homes in the City of Santa Barbara only, not condos, not the wider county. We rotate through a different market each issue.

Window Shopping

Some listings that caught my eye this issue.

3661 Sunset Drive, Santa Barbara: $2,995,000

San Roque single-level, fully reworked inside and out. French oak floors, a kitchen that means business, in-ceiling speakers, updated wiring and networking, and a backyard that got the same love as the interior. Quiet neighborhood, walkable, done right. 3 bed | 3 bath | 2,288 sqft | 0.21 acre. Listing courtesy of Aaron Gilles, Village Properties. (MLS #26-2513)

1249 Diana Lane, Santa Barbara: $3,175,000

Compact footprint, big price: proof that in this market, location and finish beat square footage every time. 3 bed | 3 bath | 1,381 sqft | 0.17 acre. Listing courtesy of Pippa Davis, Compass. (MLS #26-2488)

1461-1463 Edgecliff Lane, Montecito: $58,500,000

This one's not for browsing, it's for gawking. A gated, dual-parcel oceanfront compound with 195+ feet of Montecito coastline, four structures (main house, guest house, beach pavilion with a wellness center and art studio, plus a beach cottage), private access to Hammonds Beach, and a four-car garage, which on this stretch of coast is basically a unicorn. 9 bed | 11 bath | 8,934 sqft | 0.86 acre. Listing courtesy of Timothy Di Prizito, Christie's International RE SoCal. (MLS #26-2458)

See something you like? Reach out and let's talk. Not my listings. Sharing because they caught my eye. I'm happy to show you any of these or find something that fits even better.

This Issue's Vibe

Local adventurers, storytellers, eats & other must-follows.

Follow: @petitsoleilslo

A European-inspired boutique bed and breakfast tucked into downtown SLO. Cobblestone courtyard, nightly wine hour, the kind of place you book for a weekend and end up staying at every time you drive up the coast.

Follow: @rinconrooms

Six quiet, contactless boutique rooms in downtown Carpinteria, just opened this summer. English restraint meets coastal light, steps from Rincon. Local owners, no front desk, no pretense.

House Radio

The soundtrack to the SB Residency, updated all the time.

Everything we're listening to here in Santa Barbara, updated all the time. Listen on Spotify

On repeat this issue: BLINK (Deluxe Edition) by Bob Moses. Dropped July 10. Electronic, 14 tracks, exactly the record for a drive up the 101 with the windows down.

Currently Obsessed With: Claude AI

Whatever's got my attention this cycle: tool, trend, or otherwise.

I've been deep in it the last couple weeks. Rebuilt my website, built out a virtual assistant, set up an email checker, and yeah, this newsletter you're reading is part of it too. It's making me faster, more efficient, and more connected to my clients than I thought possible, without losing my voice in the process. If you're curious how any of it works, ask me next time we talk.

And it's not just a smarter Google. If you don't know how to do something, it'll walk you through it step by step: screenshots, explanations, the works, like having a patient expert sitting next to you instead of a search bar spitting out ten blue links you have to sort through yourself. I've had it walk me through coding, which I had zero background in going in, one step at a time until it actually worked. Basically: if you can think it, you can try it. That's been the real shift for me, not just getting answers faster, but actually building things I had no business being able to build on my own.
